A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CDCL-NLI dataset and RST-enhanced graph method. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification, cross-lingual transfer, explanation-quality, ablation, and dataset-annotation results in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical evaluations and reports revised annotation-agreement statistics and two revised classification scores.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain DM-RST parsing, XLM-RoBERTa embeddings, lexical-edge fusion, two-layer RST-GAT, EDU explanation prediction, and the same losses. The revised diagram and explanatory additions do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 25,410-instance, 26-language CDCL-NLI dataset and DocNLI, including English-only evaluation and the same five-language transfer scenarios. The newly specified translation provenance does not establish changed dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain hypothesis-only, DocNLI, R2F, Llama-3-8B, GPT-4o, and Qwen3-8B comparisons. R2F remains the transfer and explanation comparator. Newly discussed graph methods and discourse frameworks are cited but not newly evaluated.

E3.justification: Figure 13 replaces the Spanish premise in the reported one-example validation prompt with a shorter paraphrase, revising the documented LLM evaluation input. The PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun. Dataset splits, evaluation metrics, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations, single-document comparisons, language-transfer tests, threshold sensitivity analysis, and mine-disaster case study retain the same analytical questions. The new parser discussion adds rationale, without a new parser-error robustness experiment; revised ablation scores are covered under E6.

E5.justification: Section 3.4 newly specifies averaging Cohen’s kappa across three annotator pairs assigned separate training subsets. Table 6 replaces initial/final agreement reporting with a single score column, and Appendix A.3 drops quantitative post-adjudication kappa claims. Neither version reports model-run uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 3 changes English-test macro F1 from 36.12 to 35.91 for hypothesis-only and from 53.29 to 50.67 for '- Exp & Graph'; the proposed model remains at 68.95 and 70.68. Table 6 replaces initial/final kappa entries with 0.72/0.71/0.71 for entailment/neutral/contradiction and retains only the former initial explanation scores, 0.76/0.81/0.85. Other experimental tables and plotted findings are retained.

T1.justification: The task definitions, graph construction mathematics, attention equations, and loss formulations remain substantively unchanged, including Equations 1–8 and Appendix B. The added discussion of discourse-framework complexity supplies motivation rather than a new derivation or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a new CDCL-NLI task and dataset, an interpretable RST-enhanced graph method, and superior performance over the evaluated baselines. The added 'new benchmark' wording reiterates the existing contribution, while the shortened conclusion retains the central claims.

C2.justification: Section 4 newly argues that RST balances document-level structure and computational feasibility relative to PDTB and SDRT, and interprets the existing graph ablation as supporting effectiveness despite parsing errors. Section 3.4 explains the rationale for English-only annotation. The two-document applicability limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 newly identifies DeepL translation from English into 25 target languages, English-only human annotation, annotator-pair allocation, and document-source metadata. The code/data hyperlink changes from an anonymous review repository to a GitHub repository. These are documentation and access-information changes; existing hardware and training hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: New Section 2.3 substantially expands positioning around the central graph method, covering discourse-aware graphs, AMR reasoning, and prior graph merging for multi-document summarization. Section 4 adds comparison with PDTB and SDRT, and the related-work conclusion frames the contribution as systematic integration for CDCL-NLI.

P1.justification: v3 adds a related-work subsection, expands selected dataset and method explanations, shortens the conclusion, and updates author information and acknowledgments. Most prose and the overall section and appendix organization are retained rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: Figure 4 rearranges the encoder within the pipeline and expands its caption; Figure 5 corrects the module label, and Figure 2 gains an annotation clarification. Table 6 changes from initial/final columns to one score column. Figures and tables are reflowed, and the validation-prompt display is shortened; the empirical plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The expanded research context and newly disclosed construction, annotation, and access details improve documentation. However, v2’s main text and Table 6 agreed on final explanation scores, whereas v3’s Table 6 and Appendix A.3 report 0.76/0.81/0.85 while Section 3.4 retains 0.91/0.94/1.00. This unresolved discrepancy in evidence for the central dataset-quality claim prevents a reliable net improvement judgment.
